```{python}
listing("blocks.py", "_QueryTokens")
```
:::

### The prediction points' geometry {#sec-arch-interior-geometry}

**A prediction point's signed distance and direction come from the exact
closest point on the full-resolution boundary surface, so they are the same
for every draw of the boundary tokens, and they are continuous through the
surface.** Stage 3 needs a direction at every token, and the input layer
above needs a distance to the wall. Both are computed inside the model and
never taken as inputs; the model reads no stored signed-distance field.
That is Peter's boundary-only input ruling, to "just pass in the
full-resolution boundary surfaces and ONLY that": the boundary meshes
are the model's one geometric input, and every geometric quantity is
computed from them inside the forward pass. Picture a point a hair off an airfoil whose tokens kept every fifth panel:
the nearest kept token is up to a few panels away, but the nearest point of
the airfoil is directly below the point. The model therefore searches the
surface itself, the union of the cells of every given boundary mesh at full
resolution, for the closest point $p_q$ to $x_q$: point to face, never point
to centroid (`exact_boundary_geometry`).

The distance is signed by the generalized winding number $w(x_q)$ of the
oriented cells (Jacobson, Kavan and Sorkine-Hornung), the solid angle the
cells subtend at the point over that of a sphere: $\sigma$ inside a closed
surface and 0 outside it, with $\sigma = \pm 1$ the sign of the volume the
cells enclose. So $\sigma / 2 - w$ is $+1/2$ on the side the normals point to and $-1/2$ on the
other, whichever way they point. The sign needs no closest feature, so it is
right behind a sharp trailing edge, at a concave corner and at a fold, where
cells meet back to back: the two sheets of a zero-thickness fold cancel in
$w$, and both of its sides take the sign of the region around it. An open
surface is signed by the threshold $w = 1/2$. The distance is positive on the
side the cells' normals point to; the recipe orients each dataset's boundary
with a transform set per dataset file (`FlipBoundaryOrientation`). The
direction $u_q$ points from the surface to the point: the closest cell's
normal turned toward the point when $p_q$ is inside a cell, the unit
difference otherwise. Where several features tie for the closest point, as
on the medial surface (a plate's mid-plane, a corner's bisector), $u_q$ is
the point of the convex hull of their directions closest to the origin: the
least-norm element of the Clarke generalized gradient of the distance, the
midpoint of two directions and zero where they cancel. The token then reads
the distance in length units and the direction times the sign of the
distance, which is the gradient of the signed distance where it has one. @fig-arch-exact-geometry
draws both on the airfoil, with the class's own functions.

```{python}
#| label: fig-arch-exact-geometry
#| fig-cap: >
#|   The prediction points' geometry on the airfoil of @fig-arch-boundary-draw, computed by the class's
#|   `exact_boundary_geometry` and `soft_log_length` as the page renders. Top, mid-chord on both surfaces: prediction
#|   points (aqua) joined by solid lines to their exact closest points $p_q$ on the full 160-cell polyline (gray), and
#|   by dotted lines to the nearest token of two training-mode draws of 32 tokens (open and filled dots); the solid
#|   lines are the model's geometry, the dotted ones show what a nearest-token search would read instead. Bottom: the
#|   two distance channels, $s$ (aqua) and $\operatorname{asinh}(s / \varepsilon)$ (blue), against the signed
#|   distance $s$ in length units, on an axis that is linear within $\pm\varepsilon = \pm 10^{-6}$ (the gray band, where
#|   the soft logarithm is linear) and logarithmic outside. How to read this: the exact geometry does not depend on which tokens were
#|   drawn, and the soft logarithm passes through zero with a finite slope, so a point on the wall reads what its
#|   neighbors on either side read. It does not show a trained model.
#| fig-height: 6.0
#| code-fold: true
from physicsnemo.experimental.models.isla.geometry import exact_boundary_geometry, soft_log_length, LENGTH_SOFTENING
xy_g = torch.tensor(JD["xy"][:-1], dtype=torch.float64)
n_g = len(xy_g)
cells_g = torch.stack([(torch.arange(n_g) + 1) % n_g, torch.arange(n_g)], -1)   # oriented so the normals point out of the body
x0, x1 = -0.2, 0.9                                                                # the window: mid-chord, both surfaces
pick = [i for i in range(n_g) if x0 + 0.1 < JD["mid"][i, 0] < x1 - 0.1][::5]
qs = np.concatenate([JD["mid"][pick] + off * JD["nrm"][pick] for off in (0.035, 0.09)])
d_g, u_g = exact_boundary_geometry(torch.tensor(qs), xy_g, cells_g)
p_g = qs - (d_g[:, None] * torch.where((d_g >= 0)[:, None], u_g, -u_g)).numpy()
draws = [sample_boundary_cells([a_d], [x_d], BUDGET_D, torch.tensor(u0, dtype=torch.float64))[0].numpy() for u0 in (0.13, 0.71)]
fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 1, figsize=(8.0, 6.0), gridspec_kw=dict(height_ratios=[1.3, 1.0], hspace=0.3))
ax = axes[0]
ax.plot(JD["xy"][:, 0], JD["xy"][:, 1], color=MUTED, lw=1.4)
for k, (kd, mfc) in enumerate(zip(draws, (WHITE, INK))):
    tok = JD["mid"][kd]
    for q in qs:
        j = int(np.argmin(((tok - q) ** 2).sum(1)))
        ax.plot([q[0], tok[j, 0]], [q[1], tok[j, 1]], ls=":", lw=0.9, color=INK if k else MUTED)
    ax.plot(tok[:, 0], tok[:, 1], "o", ms=5, mfc=mfc, mec=INK, mew=0.8, zorder=4)
for q, p in zip(qs, p_g):
    ax.plot([q[0], p[0]], [q[1], p[1]], color=AQUA, lw=1.8)
ax.plot(qs[:, 0], qs[:, 1], "o", color=AQUA, ms=5, zorder=5)
ax.set_xlim(x0, x1); ax.set_aspect("equal"); ax.axis("off")
ax = axes[1]
s_ax = np.concatenate([-np.logspace(0, -9, 400), [0.0], np.logspace(-9, 0, 400)])
y_ax = soft_log_length(torch.tensor(s_ax)).numpy()
ax.axvspan(-LENGTH_SOFTENING, LENGTH_SOFTENING, color="#ecebe6", lw=0)
ax.plot(s_ax, y_ax, color=BLUE, lw=1.8)
ax.plot(s_ax, s_ax, color=AQUA, lw=1.4)
label_line(ax, 1e-2, float(soft_log_length(torch.tensor(1e-2))), r"$\mathrm{asinh}(s/\varepsilon)$", BLUE, dy=-3.0)
label_line(ax, 1e-2, 1e-2, r"$s$", AQUA, dy=2.0)
ax.set_xscale("symlog", linthresh=LENGTH_SOFTENING)
ax.set_xticks([-1, -1e-3, -1e-6, 0, 1e-6, 1e-3, 1]); ax.set_xticklabels(["−1", "−0.001", "−10⁻⁶", "0", "10⁻⁶", "0.001", "1"])
ax.set_xlabel("signed distance in length units $s = \\delta / L$ [–]"); ax.set_ylabel("channel value [–]")
for sp in ("top", "right"): ax.spines[sp].set_visible(False)
plt.show()
```

In symbols, with $\hat n_f$ the normal of the cell $f$ that holds $p_q$ and
$u_k$ the directions of the tied features $k$:

$$
\delta_q \equiv \operatorname{sign}\big(\tfrac{\sigma}{2} - w(x_q)\big)\, \lvert x_q - p_q \rvert,
\qquad
u_q \equiv \begin{cases}
  \operatorname{sign}\big((x_q - p_q) \cdot \hat n_f\big)\, \hat n_f & p_q \text{ inside the cell } f, \\
  \operatorname*{arg\,min}_{v \in \operatorname{conv}\{u_k\}} \lvert v \rvert & \text{at a tie,} \\
  (x_q - p_q) / \lvert x_q - p_q \rvert & \text{otherwise,}
\end{cases}
$$

$$
s_q \equiv \delta_q / L, \qquad
\big[\, s_q,\ \operatorname{asinh}(s_q / \varepsilon) \,\big], \qquad
\hat\nu_q \equiv \operatorname{sign}(\delta_q)\, u_q, \quad \operatorname{sign}(0) \equiv +1 .
$$

A point on the surface, whose float64 distance lies within the rounding
bound of that distance (its coordinates cannot tell it from a point of the
surface), takes $\delta_q = 0$ and the same rule with the unit normals of the
cells that hold it in place of the directions: the cell's normal inside a
cell, the least-norm point of the hull of the normals of the cells sharing an
edge or a vertex, with the normals computed in float64 from the coordinates
as given. Coincident vertices are welded first, so a surface stored in
pieces, one mesh per condition, has the connectivity of the surface it
describes. Inside a cell $\hat\nu_q = \hat n_f$ on both
sides of the wall, and $\operatorname{asinh}(s / \varepsilon)$ is $s /
\varepsilon$ near zero and $\operatorname{sign}(s) \log(2 \lvert s \rvert /
\varepsilon)$ far from it (`soft_log_length`): the code of a point is
continuous through the surface, so a point on it, whose distance is zero or
a rounding error of either sign, reads what the points just off it read on
either side. The softening $\varepsilon = 10^{-6}$ is a precision margin in the length
unit, not a model length: about 17 times float32's unit roundoff $2^{-24}$,
so storing the coordinates in float32 moves the channel by at most 0.065
wherever the body sits in its domain on AirfRANS with its far field and by
at most 0.036 on the DrivAerML Volume task; on AeroZoo, storage and
arithmetic together move it by at most 0.12 (results/campaigns_2026-10-23/nearwall/RESULTS.md, A3).
The search's own float32 arithmetic, with the offset $x_q - p_q$ formed in
float64 (below), adds a change at rounding level. Its consequence: the channel
is linear for distances below $10^{-6} L$, and with the whole boundary $L$
is the size of the domain. That linear part holds 19.5% of AirfRANS's drawn
points with its far field, the viscous sublayer, the buffer layer and the
start of the log layer ($y^+$ about 25 to 90, estimated from a friction
velocity that was not measured), 0.57% on the DrivAerML Volume task, 0.01%
on AeroZoo, and none on the lug or Tensile2d. The standings' trained input
layers code $\log d$: their response to a tenfold change of distance is
flat over five decades. At fixed weights a tenfold change at AirfRANS's
first nodes moves the input layer 38 times less in the linear part than in
the logarithmic one, so with the whole boundary those weights resolve the
near-wall distance on AirfRANS less finely, and a model trained with the
whole boundary does not recover it: its velocity error is largest in the
first decades off the wall, and its velocity and eddy-viscosity errors are
larger below the channel's knee than above it (@sec-limits-af-whole, @sec-oq-nearwall;
results/campaigns_2026-10-23/nearwall/RESULTS.md, A1 to A3; results/campaigns_2026-10-23/nearwall/DESIGN.md, section 4).

$\delta_q$ and $u_q$ are functions of the surface and its orientation alone:
the same for every draw of the boundary tokens, unchanged by splitting a
cell, and converging as $O(h^2)$ under refinement of a smooth surface, like
a stored signed-distance field computed from the same surface. Both are
built from a difference of positions, so $\delta_q$ is invariant and $u_q$
covariant under every rigid motion and reflection (with the cells
re-oriented so that their normals follow the map), and $\delta_q$ scales
with the geometry. $s_q = \delta_q / L$ is the same for every draw too,
since $L$ is computed from the full-resolution boundary before the draw
(stage 1).

The search runs in `forward`, where the meshes are, before the draw, at the
points' precision and outside autocast (`_closest_features`, which calls the
torch custom operator `_closest_candidates`), in the boundary's centered
frame: every coordinate less the measure-weighted centroid $c$ of the
distinct cells, rounded to the points' precision, so that float32
coordinates are centered exactly. The centroid's sums are exact fixed-point
sums, so $c$ is a function of the set of cells, not of their order. The
search's rounding then scales with the size of the boundary, not with its
distance from the origin of the raw coordinates. Every candidate distance is
computed in float64 on the cell's vertices in the lexicographic order of
their positions, with an error bound $E_k$ from the coordinates' rounding and
the arithmetic's (below), and a cell ties when its interval $[D_k - E_k, D_k + E_k]$
reaches the least upper end and its closest point is a local minimum of the
distance on the surface. In three dimensions a float32 traversal of a
bounding-volume hierarchy over the cells, the model's own cell tree, finds a
nearest cell, whose exact distance plus its bound bounds the closest
distance, and a second traversal of the same tree returns every cell within
that radius; the winding number reads the same tree, with Barill et al.'s
far-field expansion of distant nodes and exact float64 solid angles near the
point. In two dimensions a brute force over the segments, chunked over the
points, keeps the candidates. The interior task is implemented in two and
three dimensions. The search runs without gradient;
the offset $x_q - p_q$ is then formed in float64 from the point and its
cell's vertices, with the barycentric weights of its region of the cell,
and rounded once to the points' precision, so $\delta_q$ and $u_q$ are
differentiable in the points and the vertex positions.

A cell of zero area, whose vertices coincide or lie on one line, is read as
the segment or the point its vertices span. Such a cell never supplies a
normal or an on-wall direction, and its winding contribution is zero. A
zero-area cell lying along the edges or at the vertices of the other cells is
left out, so the outputs are those of the mesh without it. The test is exact,
with no tolerance, for every float32 coordinate and for float64 coordinates of
magnitude between $2^{-485}$ and $2^{510}$: a float64 filter with a bound on its rounding error
clears most cells, and the cells it leaves get exact products. Every input
without such a cell gives bitwise the outputs it gave before the test, and on
the DrivAerML Volume task's whole boundary of 16.65 million cells the test
costs 2.4 ms. None of the 36 million cells of the real cases checked has two
coincident vertices, and none of the 16.65 million cells of that boundary has
zero area (results/campaigns_2026-10-23/geo_fast/FINAL_REPORT.md;
results/campaigns_2026-10-23/geo_degen/RESULTS.md).

**A thin cell of nonzero area is searched and measured to bounds on its own
rounding.** A sliver or a needle, a cell whose altitude over its longest
edge is a small fraction $\rho$ of that edge, defeats arithmetic that is
accurate on an ordinary cell. A rounded sign test of an edge plane's outward
side reads rounding where the cell's normal is uncertain, and the closest
point's barycentric weights, ratios of determinants of size $\rho^2$ built
from products of order one, move the point along the face by about the unit
roundoff over $\rho^2$, relative to the cell. Left alone, either can leave a
query with no candidate, return a farther cell or a wrong distance, or take
a point on the wall as off it: on a cube with a thin cap or needle in one
face, rotated and shifted, that starts at $\rho \approx 10^{-5}$ in float32
(a needle; a cap from $10^{-6}$) and at $\rho \approx 10^{-3}$ in float64.
The class does three things. Each edge plane of the float32 lower bound is
outward by the cell's vertex order alone, built from the cell's normal, and
a cell whose float64 normal is not accurate to its own float32 rounding, by
an a-priori bound on the cross product's rounding, gets no planes, so they
never reject it. The float64 ball test rejects a cell only when its
computed distance less a bound on that distance's error still exceeds the
radius. The closest point is misplaced along the face by at most
$\Delta = K u_{64} l^2 / (\rho^2 L_k)$, with $u_{64} = 2^{-53}$, $L_k$
the cell's longest edge, $l$ the query's greatest distance to the cell's
vertices, and $\rho$ replaced by a certified lower bound; the distance's
error bound is the smaller of $\Delta$ and $\Delta^2 / (2(\tilde d -
\Delta))$, with $\tilde d$ the computed distance, and is unbounded where
$\Delta$ exceeds $L_k$. Where that bound reaches one unit of the
distance's arithmetic bound,
$u_{64}(\lvert x' \rvert + R'_k)$, with primes for the centered frame and
$R'_k$ the greatest distance of the cell's vertices from $c$,
the class also computes the closest point accurately, in the frame of the
cell's longest edge, and takes it when the two distances differ by more
than one unit. The reference search and the fast one run the same
arithmetic and stay bitwise equal.

**Every constant of the bands and the switch is a derived worst case.**
Each candidate distance $D_k$ carries the band

$$
E_k \equiv u\,(\lvert x \rvert + R_k) + C\,u_{64}\,(\lvert x' \rvert + R'_k),
$$

with $u$ the unit roundoff of the points' precision, $R_k$ the greatest norm
of the cell's vertices, and primes for the centered frame. The first term is
the rounding of the coordinates as they were given, so it is measured in the
frame they were given in: a case placed far from the origin is rounded more
coarsely, and a storage term measured about the centroid is not a bound on
that rounding. The second is the float64 arithmetic's, measured in the
centered frame it runs in.

```{python}
#| label: para-arch-bands
#| output: asis
from physicsnemo.experimental.models.isla import geometry as _geo
GBD = " ".join(R.load("geo_band_final", "DERIVATION.md").split())
GBR = " ".join(R.load("geo_band_final", "RESULTS.md").split())
C3, C2 = _geo._BAND_UNITS[3], _geo._BAND_UNITS[2]
FOOT, SWITCH, K_ = _geo._FOOT_UNITS, _geo._SWITCH_UNITS, _geo._ERICSON_K
KEPT = SWITCH + FOOT
assert C3 == KEPT + 3 and "**C3 = 91**" in GBD and "**C2 = 17**" in GBD and f"`_FOOT_UNITS = {FOOT}`" in GBD
assert re.search(r"Two dimensions: an edge point, 15, plus the centring: 16", GBD)
K_OBS = re.search(r"largest observed ratio ([\d.]+) of the bound over 600k thin pairs", GBD).group(1)
FOOT_OBS = re.search(r"largest error observed against exact rational arithmetic is ([\d.]+)", inspect.getsource(_geo)).group(1)
BF = re.search(r"The review counted `e_bf \+ A = ([\d.]+) > (\d+)` for float64 queries", GBD).groups()
# the margin the code allows, read from the brute force's prefilter in geometry.py
BF_CODE = int(re.search(r"rounding = (\d+) \* torch\.finfo\(query_points\.dtype\)\.eps / 2", inspect.getsource(_geo)).group(1))
assert BF_CODE >= float(BF[0]) > int(BF[1])
F32_SHARE = re.search(r"the storage term u32 \(\|x\| \+ R_k\) is 1 - ([\d.]+e-\d+) of the band", GBR).group(1)
print(f"$C$ is {C3} in three dimensions and {C2} in two: the worst case, over every path the closest point's weights take, "
      "of the float64 distance's error. The greatest path is a guarded pair that keeps Ericson's point: within the switch's "
      f"{SWITCH} unit of the accurate point, whose own worst case is {FOOT} units (at a face whose exact foot rounding "
      f"rejects), and so within {KEPT} units of the exact distance. One unit more covers the centering, and two the "
      "second-order terms and the band's own evaluation. In two dimensions the only path is an edge point, 15 units, and one unit for the centering and one for the rest "
      "give 17. A "
      "count of every rounding to first order becomes a worst case once each product of two error terms is bounded and no "
      "term is divided by a quantity that rounding can make small (Higham's $\\gamma_n$); the ball test's "
      f"$K = {K_:.0f}$ is the worst case 167.25, rounded up, in the same way. The switch needs no bound of its own: any "
      f"threshold $\\tau$ is certified once $C \\ge \\tau + {FOOT + 1}$, so the band covers both branches by "
      "construction. Each constant is derived from the rounding of every operation as coded and was derived again "
      "independently. Against exact rational arithmetic on about 600,000 thin pairs, the largest error of Ericson's point "
      f"is {K_OBS} of the bound $K$ gives, and that of the accurate point {FOOT_OBS} units. The two derivations differ on "
      "one count: the margin of the two-dimensional brute force's prefilter for float64 points. The second counts "
      f"{BF[0]} units; the first counts the arithmetic share inside the error bounds the prefilter adds as well and finds "
      f"{BF[1]} enough. The code allows {BF_CODE} units, which covers both counts. The count concerns which candidates the "
      "prefilter keeps beyond the band, not an output, and for float32 points both counts leave a wide margin. For float32 points, and bfloat16 ones cast to float32, the arithmetic "
      f"share is {sci(float(F32_SHARE))} of the band; for float64 points it is most of the band "
      f"({R.source('geo_band_final', 'DERIVATION.md')}; {R.source('geo_band_final', 'REVIEW_DERIVATION.md')}).")
```

**On every dataset whose ISLA reads the interior geometry, the thin-cell treatment
changes nothing the model sees.**
The distance, the direction, the winding sign, the tie and on-wall
decisions and every gradient are bitwise those of the same search without
it, under both kernels, on AirfRANS with its far field, AeroZoo, the lug,
Tensile2d and the DrivAerML Volume task's whole boundary; the surface
tasks compute no interior geometry. Only the op's
internal closest-point weights differ, at 11 of the 200,000 queries of a
DrivAerML whole-boundary draw, on-wall queries on ordinary cells of the
tunnel floor, by one or two units in the last place. A census of every
stored boundary mesh finds no dataset exposed: of 310,545 queries of the
recipe's draws checked against an exact rational brute force, none is
wrong, in float32 or float64, under either kernel, and no stored mesh holds
a cell whose float64 normal is uncertain. Adversarial float64 queries on
the thinnest faces of the stored AeroZoo meshes, which make the search
without the treatment raise (a device-side assert on CUDA), are answered
correctly, and of 517,296 queries of the adversarial thin-cell sets
checked on the CPU none raises or has a wrong distance, cell, on-wall
decision or sign. The treatment's cost is in @sec-using-cost
(results/campaigns_2026-10-23/geo_thin_final/RESULTS.md, A1 to A3, "Phase C checks" and
"Final head").

```{python}

print("**The derived bands, the centered frame, the certified tie test and the float64 offset move the geometry at "

      "one RMS radius of the boundary, the points whose tie set changes number "
      f"{LUG_P[2]} over the 20 lug cases measured, against {LUG_P[1]} under a bitwise test of distinct directions, and "
      f"{T2D_P[1]} on Tensile2d, against {T2D_P[0]}; the direction moves by at most {sci(float(LUG_P[0]))} at those lug "
      f"points. On DrivAerML's whole boundary the points whose direction moves by more than $10^{{-3}}$ number "
      f"{int(DRV_E[1]):,} of 400,000, against {int(DRV_E[0]):,} under the first-order bands and the bitwise test, each a "
      "point at a band's edge whose move lies within its certified direction uncertainty. With a case translated by $L$ and a softening a thousand times smaller than the channel's, the search's "
      "own float32 rounding changes the distance channel by "
      f"{sci(float(FAR[1]))} at the 99.9th percentile on DrivAerML's whole boundary, against {FAR[0]} with the offset "
      "$x_q - p_q$ formed in float32 from the raw coordinates; centering the search's arithmetic alone does not change it. "
      "The reference and the fast search stay bitwise equal. Read through this geometry, the "
      f"{S._COUNT[len(IC_RUNS)]} ISLA models trained with the class's tie rule on the lug and Tensile2d change their case-mean "
      f"errors by at most {sci(IC_LOG)} in the logarithm and their posed ÷ native by at most {sci(IC_PN)}, so the "
      "pre-registered check reads no retraining. The cost is in @sec-using-cost "

      f"{R.source('geo_band_final', 'INFER_CHECK.md')}).")
```

**Four kinds of input remain limits of the search**, each measured on the
stored meshes: overlapping coplanar cells, T-junctions, near-duplicate
normals at a tie, and the inputs' own rounding at a band's edge. **Cells that
overlap in one plane**, of zero area or not, change
the direction at ties, since each joins the tie set: on a closed box with
triangles of nonzero area added inside its faces, 891 of 9,768 float32
queries change their direction, and a cell reversed inside a face cancels
in the winding number by the fold rule and flips the sign of the distance
near it. The stored meshes hold no coplanar fold and no overlap in an axis
plane; AeroZoo's recipe dump has 4 near folds, $3 \times 10^{-4}$ rad from
flat, and the recipe's queries near them get bitwise the same distance and
direction without the thinner cell. **T-junctions**, vertices that lie on
another cell's edge, number 110 on 74 edges of the tunnel floor of the
DrivAerML Volume task's whole boundary: none of the 200,000 queries of a
draw has its closest point at one, and with every cell over such an edge
split at its T-junctions the distance, the direction and the sign are
bitwise unchanged at all of them (results/campaigns_2026-10-23/geo_degen/RESULTS.md,
check b; results/campaigns_2026-10-23/geo_thin_final/RESULTS.md, A1 to A3 and T-junctions).
The other two are limits of the tie rule, below.

**Where the tied directions are certified distinct, no step of this
geometry is left to the order of a search or to the sign of a cancelling
sum.** The direction at such a tie is a function of the tie set
alone, not of the order of the vertices, the cells or the search, and a flip
of the boundary's winding negates $\delta_q$ and $\operatorname{sign}(\delta_q)\,
u_q$ bitwise. A point is tied only when two of its tied features' directions
are certified distinct: farther apart than the sum of bounds on their
rounding, each $\sqrt 2$ times a bound on the sine of the computed
direction's error (2 where that bound reaches 1). Directions that agree to
within their rounding, such as the normals of a planar star of cells, do not
make a tie; on the wall the direction is then the normal of the cell of least
index among those at the least distance, so it follows the cells' order, and
since the certification's bound scales with the queries' precision, a float32
point and its float64 copy can differ there (@sec-limits-tie-order). What
rounding still decides is which features join a tie set,
since a feature joins when its distance lies within the rounding bound of the
least; and where the normals of a tie nearly coincide, as on a structured
mesh's split faces, their least-norm point is ill-conditioned, so its float32
and float64 values differ. It is Hölder-continuous of order 1/2 in the
normals: where two of them are within about the square root of their
rounding of each other, rounding picks which of them the least-norm point
rests on, and the value is the least-norm point either way. On the lug and
Tensile2d, a random one-ulp move of every float32 vertex changes the
direction at tied queries by at most $3.9 \times 10^{-5}$ and
$6.4 \times 10^{-6}$, at most 2.6 times the normals' own change, and changes
the set of normals it rests on at no persisting tie (results/campaigns_2026-10-23/geo_thin_final/RESULTS.md, A4).

**A case's float32 rounding grows with its distance from the origin, so a
point at a band's edge can change its decision under a translation.** The
band's storage term bounds the rounding of the coordinates as they were
given. A pose that moves the case away from the origin rounds them more
coarsely, so no band that bounds that rounding stays fixed under a
translation, and a rotation alone moves the gap between two features by about
the band, so no threshold rule is free of such flips. Each flip answers the
point correctly for its own inputs: in each pose the class decides from the
coordinates it is given.

```{python}
#| label: para-arch-band-edge
#| output: asis
GTR_ = " ".join(R.load("geo_thin_final", "RESULTS.md").split())
GAP_ = re.search(r"Gap over band ([\d.]+) \(untied: u the face normal\) against ([\d.]+) \(tied", GTR_).groups()
DU_, NODES_ = re.search(r"\|du\| = ([\d.]+) at that one node of ([\d,]+), which is the whole forward excess", GTR_).groups()
VF_ = re.search(r"\| VF \| ([\d.]+e-\d+), ([\d.]+e-\d+) \(1884\) \| ([\d.]+e-\d+), ([\d.]+e-\d+) \|", GBR).groups()
DRV_T1 = re.search(r"\| DrivAerML whole \| 1 \| ([\d,]+) \(([\d.]+)\), ([\d,]+), 0 \| ([\d,]+), ([\d,]+), 0 \|", GBR).groups()
AF_T1 = re.search(r"\| AirfRANS \+ far field \| 1 \| [\d,]+, [\d,]+, ([\d,]+) \| [\d,]+, [\d,]+, ([\d,]+) \| [\d,]+, [\d,]+, [\d,]+ \|", GBR).groups()
assert AF_T1[0] == AF_T1[1]
AF_RMS = re.search(r"whose boundary RMS radius is (\d+) chords", GBR).group(1)
AF_ROUND, AF_FIRST = re.search(r"the storage rounding \(about ([\d.e-]+) chords\) exceeds the first nodes' distance from the airfoil \(([\d.e-]+) chords\)", GBR).groups()
print(f"On the lug's test case 1884 one node of {NODES_} lies at the edge: the gap between its two nearest features is "
      f"{GAP_[0]} times the sum of their bands natively and {GAP_[1]} times it rotated and translated, so it ties in one pose "
      f"only and its direction moves by {DU_}. That node carries the whole excess of the posed change of an ISLA-DTT forward "
      f"with random weights, read through the forest built outside autocast (@sec-arch-tree-read), on that case, {sci(float(VF_[1]))} relative RMS against a median of {sci(float(VF_[0]))} over "
      f"24 lug cases. On the DrivAerML Volume task's whole boundary such points number "
      f"{int(DRV_T1[3].replace(',', '')):,} of 400,000 (above). The extreme case is AirfRANS with its far field, "
      f"whose boundary's RMS radius is {AF_RMS} chords: rotated and translated by that radius, its coordinates are rounded to about "
      f"{sci(float(AF_ROUND))} chords, more than the first nodes' distance from the airfoil, {sci(float(AF_FIRST))} chords, so {AF_T1[0]} of "
      "the 400,000 drawn points (four draws), all near the wall, are read as on the wall, whatever the frame of the arithmetic. Their coordinates "
      "cannot tell them from the wall. The scoring protocol's pose of AirfRANS, a rotation and a translation by one RMS radius "
      f"of the interior points, is milder: an ISLA-DTT forward with random weights and the same forest changes its pressure by at most "
      f"{sci(float(VF_[3]))} relative RMS over 24 cases, {sci(float(VF_[2]))} in the median (@sec-medial-ties measures what the geometry does to the contracts, and "
      "@sec-standing-geometry gives the geometry the standings' checkpoints were trained with; "
      f"{R.source('geo_thin_final', 'RESULTS.md')}, \"Fourth limit\"; {R.source('geo_band_final', 'RESULTS.md')}, item 2).")
```

```{python}
#| label: para-arch-sdf-configs

def _model_block(name):
    cfg = yaml.safe_load((CONF / f"{name}.yaml").read_text())
    blk = dict(cfg.get("model", {}))
    for parent in cfg.get("defaults", []) or []:
        if isinstance(parent, str):
            base = yaml.safe_load((CONF / f"{parent}.yaml").read_text()).get("model", {})
            blk = {**base, **blk}
    return cfg, blk
interior_cfgs = sorted(p.stem for p in CONF.glob("isla_*.yaml") if _model_block(p.stem)[1].get("interior"))
fmt = lambda xs: ", ".join(f"`{x}`" for x in xs)
print(f"The prediction points' only input is their positions. The recipe's interior ISLA configurations are "
      f"{fmt(interior_cfgs)} (read from `conf/model/` as the page renders), and none of them gives ISLA a stored "
      "signed-distance field.")
```

**What the exact geometry measures.** Two pre-registered comparisons
isolate this stage (@tbl-arch-geo-evidence), the first on the AirfRANS
interior task, the second on it and on PLAID Tensile2d and the GINOT lug. The
first replaces the nearest-token geometry of the nearest-token form
(@sec-checkpoint-form) by the exact geometry, read through a signed
logarithm $\operatorname{sign}(s_q) \log(\lvert s_q \rvert + 10^{-12})$;
the second keeps the exact geometry and replaces that channel by
$\operatorname{asinh}(s_q / \varepsilon)$ and the direction $u_q$ by
$\operatorname{sign}(\delta_q)\, u_q$, the encoding above. Every arm
except the first comparison's control reads the exact built-in geometry,
and every arm is otherwise of the nearest-token form: it still reads the
stored signed distance and its direction as a prediction-point input on all
three datasets (the second comparison's variant encodes that channel as it
encodes $s_q$). The class reads no stored field, so neither comparison is a
measurement of the class; they are the registered tests that chose the
design, and @tbl-arch-attrib, below, measures the class. Chapter 4 gives what
the exact geometry does to the contracts (@sec-exact-geometry-draw,
@sec-medial-ties).

```{python}
#| label: tbl-arch-geo-evidence
#| output: asis
GE = json.load(open(RES / "campaigns_2026-10-19" / "geo_evidence" / "geo_evidence.json"))
g1, gc = GE["geo1_airfrans"], GE["geo_cont"]
AFF = (("pressure_l2", "pressure"), ("velocity_l2", "velocity"), ("nut_l2", "eddy viscosity"))
def seeds_of(arm, f):
    return [arm[f]["per_seed"][s] for s in ("42", "43")]
def row(label, var, ctl, f, fname, in_rule):
    v, c = seeds_of(var, f), seeds_of(ctl, f)
    r = np.mean(v) / np.mean(c)
    side = "below" if max(v) < min(c) else ("above" if min(v) > max(c) else "overlap")
    return f"| {label} | {fname} | {np.mean(c):.5f} | {np.mean(v):.5f} | {r:.3f} | {' / '.join(f'{x / y:.3f}' for x, y in zip(v, c))} | {side} | {in_rule} |\n"
out = ("| comparison (variant ÷ control) | field | control | variant | ratio | per seed | variant seeds vs control seeds | in the registered rule |\n"
       "|---|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|---|---|\n")
for f, fname in AFF:
    out += row("exact geometry ÷ nearest-token geometry, AirfRANS", g1["geo1"]["native"], g1["a2s"]["native"], f, fname, "–")
dec = []
for ds, lab, fields in (("af", "AirfRANS", AFF), ("t2dz", "PLAID Tensile2d", (("displacement_l2", "displacement"), ("stress_l2", "stress"), ("q_l2", "q"))),
                        ("lug", "GINOT lug", (("von_mises_l2", "von Mises stress"),))):
    for f, fname in fields:
        rule = "yes" if (ds == "af" or f == "displacement_l2") else "no"
        if rule == "yes":
            dec.append(gc[ds]["cont_over_ctl"]["native"][f])
        out += row(f"continuous encoding ÷ signed-log encoding, {lab}", gc[ds]["cont"]["native"], gc[ds]["ctl"]["native"], f, fname, rule)
print(out)
G_dec = float(np.exp(np.mean(np.log(dec))))
print(f": The exact-geometry evidence: area-weighted relative L2 of each control and variant, seed means of two seeds (42, 43) "
      f"and the per-seed ratios paired by seed, native meshes, float32, final checkpoints. Instrument: ISLA at the reference "
      f"configuration with the normalized slice reads, both arms of a comparison trained alike, every arm reading the stored "
      f"signed distance as a prediction-point input beside its built-in geometry; AirfRANS uniform interior "
      f"task, 200 test cases; PLAID Tensile2d and the GINOT lug on their interior tasks. Results: "
      f"results/campaigns_2026-10-19/geo_evidence/geo_evidence.json (`geo1_airfrans`, `geo_cont`). How to read this: a "
      f"ratio compares two ISLA variants, the variant over its control, and below one means the variant is more accurate; "
      f"\"below\" means both variant seeds lie below both control seeds. The registered rule of the second comparison read "
      f"its four marked fields: their geometric mean ratio is {G_dec:.3f}, inside its adoption bar (at most 1.01, with no field "
      f"at 1.10 or more); the other fields were reported beside the rule. The first comparison's control is the standing's "
      f"ISLA arm, of the nearest-token form (@sec-checkpoint-form). The table does not compare ISLA with a baseline.")
```

```{python}
    return all(max(seeds_of(var, f)) < min(seeds_of(ctl, f)) for f, _ in fields)
r1 = g1["geo1_over_a2s"]["native"]; r2 = gc["af"]["cont_over_ctl"]["native"]; rl = gc["lug"]["cont_over_ctl"]["native"]["von_mises_l2"]
```

### The read-only interior task {#sec-arch-passive-decoder}

**On the interior task (ISLA-DTT) the
prediction points are read-only: at every slice layer they read the slices the boundary formed at
that layer and never write into them, and after it they read the boundary
cells (@sec-arch-global-read), so the prediction at a point is a function
of that point and the boundary alone.** A read-only point is encoded
with its exact geometry and its own input layer `qt.seed`,
and runs through the same twelve slice layers with
the same parameters as the boundary tokens. Only its measure bias differs:
$\ell_q = -\infty$, so every softmax over tokens gives it zero weight. It
takes no part in the routing prototypes, the anchors $z_s, m_s$ (step c),
the routing weights $a_{is}$ (step f), the slice states $Z_s$ (step g) or
the head frame's anchors (stage 4). It still forms its own logits, its
relational invariants against the anchors and its read-back weights
$\pi_{qs}$, and it reads $b_q = \sum_s \pi_{qs} Z_s$ (step h). The boundary
tokens therefore compute what they compute in the surface task whatever
points are requested, and a request split into chunks, permuted, or reduced
to one point returns the same predictions to $10^{-12}$ in float64
(`test_interior_task_contracts`). On the AirfRANS standing's
checkpoints, trained without compilation, in float32 every change of the request of
@tbl-query-population moves ISLA-DTT's error by at most
`{python} Markdown(sci(DTT_QDEV))`, float32 roundoff. ISLA-DTT has no routing-mass
parameter.

A read-only point reads at matched depth: at layer $\ell$ it reads the
slices formed from the boundary states at layer $\ell$, the depth its own
state has reached. That alignment accounts for much of the read-only model's
accuracy. @tbl-arch-read-depth isolates it on read-only points without the
boundary read: a control with the same parameters, in which every layer's
points read slices formed from the *final* boundary state, is markedly less
accurate on both interior datasets, while doubling the slice count changes
neither the read-only nor the interacting model beyond seed noise.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-arch-read-depth
#| output: asis
REPORT = (RESEARCH / "dtt" / "REPORT.md").read_text()
def md_section_table(title_prefix):
    sec = REPORT.split("\n### ")
    body = next(s for s in sec if s.startswith(title_prefix))
    rows = [l for l in body.splitlines() if l.startswith("| ") and not l.startswith("| arm") and not l.startswith("|---")]
    return {r.split("|")[1].strip(): [c.strip() for c in r.split("|")[2:-1]] for r in rows}
def triple(s):
    return [float(x) for x in s.split(" / ")]
af = md_section_table("E6 interim on AirfRANS"); car = md_section_table("E6 interim on the car")
pick = lambda t, pref: next(v for k, v in t.items() if k.startswith(pref))
ROWS = [("read-only points, matched depth (base)", "P, 512 slices (E3)", "P, 256 slices (E5)", "P"),
        ("read-only points reading the final boundary state", "FINAL control", "FINAL control", "P"),
        ("read-only points, twice the slices", "P, 1,024 slices", "P, 512 slices", "P"),
        ("interacting points (base)", "I, 512 slices", "I, 256 slices (E5)", "I"),
        ("interacting points, twice the slices", "I, 1,024 slices", "I, 512 slices", "I")]
base = {("car", "P"): triple(pick(car, "P, 512 slices (E3)")[2]), ("af", "P"): triple(pick(af, "P, 256 slices (E5)")[2]),
        ("car", "I"): triple(pick(car, "I, 512 slices")[2]), ("af", "I"): triple(pick(af, "I, 256 slices (E5)")[2])}
fmt3 = lambda v: " / ".join(f"{x:.4f}" for x in v)
out = "| model | DrivAerML Volume: p / v / nut | ÷ its base | AirfRANS: p / v / nut | ÷ its base |\n|---|---|---|---|---|\n"
for lab, kc, ka, kind in ROWS:
    vc, va = triple(pick(car, kc)[2]), triple(pick(af, ka)[2])
    rc = " / ".join(f"{x / y:.2f}" for x, y in zip(vc, base[("car", kind)]))
    ra = " / ".join(f"{x / y:.2f}" for x, y in zip(va, base[("af", kind)]))
    out += f"| {lab} | {fmt3(vc)} | {rc} | {fmt3(va)} | {ra} |\n"
print(out)
print(": Matched-depth reading and slice count, without the boundary read: relative L2 of interior pressure / "
      "velocity / eddy viscosity (p / v / nut), float32, seed means of two seeds (42, 43). DrivAerML Volume task: 48 held-out "
      "cars, 200,000 boundary cells and 200,000 prediction points per car; AirfRANS interior task: 200 test airfoils, "
      "100,000 prediction points from one contiguous window of the stored points, so ratios compare like with like and the "
      "absolute errors do not carry over (@sec-interior-airfrans). Instrument: on the car, ISLA at 512 wide, 512 slices "
      "(1,024 doubled), 3.75e-4, raw slice reads; on the airfoil, ISLA at 384 wide, 256 slices (512 doubled), 5e-4, raw slice "
      "reads (@sec-study-configurations); checkpoints of the nearest-token form (@sec-checkpoint-form). How to read this: each ÷ compares a row with the base row of its own kind (read-only "
      "or interacting) on the same dataset, above one meaning less accurate; the second row changes only which boundary state "
      "the points read, the third and fifth only the slice count; the two interacting car rows were trained on code that differs "
      "beyond the slice count, so their ratio is not a clean slice-count effect. Data: research/dtt/REPORT.md, its "
      "matched-depth sections on AirfRANS and on the car.")
```

#### The global boundary read {#sec-arch-global-read}

**A read-only point also reads the boundary cells themselves: after every
slice layer each prediction point adds a measure-weighted average of the
cells' states over the whole boundary, weighted by a learned kernel of where
each cell sits relative to the point and by how well their states
match.** For a point $q$ and a cell $j$, with $\rho_{qj} \equiv r_q - r_j$,
the kernel sees the pair's invariants $\iota_{qj}$: the distance
$\lvert\rho_{qj}\rvert$, its logarithm, $\log(\lvert\rho_{qj}\rvert /
\lvert s_q\rvert)$ (the distance in units of the point's own distance to
the surface), the cosines of $\hat\rho_{qj}$ with $\hat n_j$, $\hat\nu_q$
and every $\hat g_k$, and $\hat\nu_q \cdot \hat n_j$ and $\hat n_j \cdot
\hat g_k$; each of the cell's shared vector channels $V_{ja}$ adds its
cosines with $\hat\rho_{qj}$ and $\hat\nu_q$ (`tree_pair_invariants`). One MLP shared by every layer maps $\iota_{qj}$ to
a basis of kernel functions per pair, once per forward pass
(`_KernelBasis`), and each layer's kernel $\kappa_h$ is a learned
combination of them for each head $h$. With $\omega_j \equiv w_j / \sum_i
w_i$ the cell's share of the boundary measure, $\tilde h \equiv
\mathrm{LN}(h)$ (one LayerNorm for cells, one for points) and $c$ key
channels per head, the read after a layer is

$$
\alpha_{qjh} = \operatorname*{softmax}_j \Big( \kappa_h(\iota_{qj})
  + \tfrac{1}{\sqrt{c}} \big\langle W^{\mathrm q}_h \tilde h_q,\ W^{\mathrm k}_h \tilde h_j \big\rangle
  + \log \omega_j \Big),
\qquad
h_q \leftarrow h_q + W^{\mathrm o} \Big[ \textstyle\sum_j \alpha_{qjh}\, W^{\mathrm v}_h \tilde h_j \Big]_{h} ,
$$

where the brackets concatenate the heads' value channels and $W^{\mathrm
o}$ starts at zero, so training begins from the model without the read.

```{python}
#| label: para-arch-read-constants
#| output: asis
import physicsnemo.experimental.models.isla.tree_read as TR
print(f"The read's constants are fixed in the class: {TR.KERNEL_READ_BASIS} kernel basis functions "
      f"(`KERNEL_READ_BASIS`), {TR.KERNEL_READ_HEADS} heads (`KERNEL_READ_HEADS`), $c = {TR.KERNEL_READ_KEY}$ key channels "
      f"per head (`KERNEL_READ_KEY`) and {TR.KERNEL_READ_WIDTH // TR.KERNEL_READ_HEADS} value channels per head "
      f"(`KERNEL_READ_WIDTH` ÷ `KERNEL_READ_HEADS`).")
```

The log measure fraction makes the read a quadrature
(@sec-isla-quadrature): with the kernel and key terms constant it is the
measure-weighted mean of the cells' values, and splitting a cell into two
coincident halves or rescaling every measure changes nothing
(`test_tree_read_similarity_refinement_and_measure_scale_at_theta_zero`).
Every input is an invariant, so the read keeps the contracts of
@sec-isla-contracts, and it leaves the boundary tokens and the slices
untouched, so it keeps query independence
(`test_tree_read_is_exactly_query_independent_at_every_theta`). Evaluated
pair by pair it costs $Q \times N$ pairs per layer: $4 \times 10^{10}$ for
200,000 points around a 200,000-cell car.

#### The read through a cluster forest {#sec-arch-tree-read}

**The read runs through a Barnes–Hut forest at the opening angle $\theta =
1$: a point reads nearby cells one by one and each distant cluster of
similarly oriented cells as one virtual cell, which keeps the prediction
exactly query-independent and pose-invariant; the frame the forest is
built in only groups cells for speed.** ISLA-DTT is ISLA with read-only prediction points, the global
read after every layer and the forest at $\theta = 1$, all set by
`interior=True`. The forest is built once per case, without
gradient (`BoundaryForest`):

1. The frame is the boundary's own canonical frame: centered on the cells'
   measure-weighted centroid, with the principal axes of their
   measure-weighted position covariance, each signed so that the third
   moment of the positions along it is positive (`canonical_frame`). The
   forest is built in these coordinates, so it moves with the body. This is
   the one place in the class where a center and axes are estimated, and
   they decide only which cells share a cluster. No learned map reads them,
   so a tie of the frame does not make the prediction jump by $O(1)$, as it
   does for a network fed canonical coordinates (@sec-landscape-symmetry).
2. The cells are split by the sign octant of their normal in that frame,
   and one cluster tree is built per octant
   (`physicsnemo.mesh.spatial.ClusterTree`, which bisects the boxes of a
   Morton space-filling curve down to leaves of `TREE_READ_LEAF_SIZE`
   cells). Opposite normals never share a tree, so no cluster spans both
   faces of a thin body.
3. Every node holds a virtual cell: its cells' measure-weighted centroid,
   their renormalized measure-weighted mean normal, their mean vector
   channels and their total measure, and at every layer the
   measure-weighted means of their keys and values. The means are sums over
   a tree of pairwise sums in the working precision, float64 in a float64
   model and float32 otherwise, bfloat16 rows included (`node_means`), so a
   float64 model reads its clusters in float64 throughout.
4. Each point walks every tree once. A node is read as one virtual cell
   when its box diagonal is below $\theta$ times the distance from the point
   to the box and its normals are coherent: their measure-weighted RMS chord
   about the mean, $\sqrt{2(1 - \lvert \bar n \rvert)}$, is below $\theta$. A
   leaf that fails either test is read cell by cell, and any other node
   hands the point to its two children, so every cell is read exactly once,
   alone or inside one virtual cell
   (`test_point_pairs_admit_only_separated_coherent_nodes_and_cover_every_cell`).
   At $\theta \geq 0.919$ in three dimensions, and $0.765$ in two, the
   coherence test admits every node: inside one sign octant
   $\lvert \bar n \rvert \geq 1/\sqrt d$, so at $\theta = 1$ the box test
   alone decides which clusters a point reads.

The softmax of the global read then runs over each point's list, a virtual
cell entering with its total measure fraction as its log bias and its
invariants computed from its centroid and normal. Because the read is a
quadrature, a virtual cell is its cluster's monopole: were the logit
constant over the cluster, reading the virtual cell would equal reading its
cells one by one. How the build, the walk and the read run on a GPU is
@sec-arch-tree-exec.

**Under bfloat16 autocast, as in training, the forest is built from rounded
coordinates.** The two products `points @ frame` in `BoundaryForest.build`
and `point_pairs` run under the caller's autocast, which casts both factors
to bfloat16, the 16-bit format training runs in, and rounds the product to
it. The trees' coordinates and boxes and the node measures are then
bfloat16, while the box diameters and the walk's box table stay float32, so
a bfloat16 training step and a float32 score of the same case build
different forests. The node measures are the denominators of every node's
mean key and value, which bfloat16 scales by up to $2^{-9}$, and they shift
the nodes' log measures by up to $2^{-9}$, so a node no longer reads exactly
as its cells do on a constant. On the AirfRANS interior task and the
lug, 82% and 99% of the points get a different list, and reading the
training forest changes the float32 native error by 0.2 to 0.7% (pressure
level). That forest is not pose-invariant: on the rotated and translated
lug, reading it gives 1.90 times the error of reading the float32 forest
(1.95 and 1.85, seeds 42 and 43), and on AirfRANS 1.012 to 1.033 times.
Each of the two candidate causes breaks pose on its own. With the octant
labels held at the native float32 ones and the box test given its error band,
the float32 product about the origin of the raw coordinates, rounded to
bfloat16, changes the list of nearly every posed point of the lug (the median
over cases 100%, at least 98%) and of 87% of AirfRANS's (the median), and the cast of the two factors to bfloat16 before the product
does the same; the same product about the boundary's centroid, rounded to
bfloat16, changes the list of one point (the median over cases) on the lug
and four on AirfRANS. The canonical frame itself moves with the body to
rounding: posed and native canonical coordinates of the lug differ by at
most $2.6 \times 10^{-7}$ of its extent, and no axis changes sign
(results/campaigns_2026-10-23/dtt_knobs/treeprec/treeprec_table.md;
results/campaigns_2026-10-23/dtt_pose/MECHANISMS.md, sections 1 and 2).

::: {.callout-note title="In flight"}
This limit is that of the code as it is. The forest built outside autocast
(below) removes it and changes ISLA-DTT's function; ISLA-DTT retrained with
it on the lug and the AirfRANS interior task is being measured, and the
ledger (@sec-ledger) tracks it.
:::

Three properties hold by construction. At $\theta = 0$, a setting of the
tests, no cluster is admitted and the read is the read of every cell pair
by pair (`test_tree_read_at_theta_zero_is_the_exact_read`). At every
$\theta$ a point's list depends on the forest and the point alone, so the
prediction is query-independent. And in exact arithmetic a rotation,
reflection or translation of the case gives the same forest and the same
lists, which the float64 test checks
(`test_forest_and_every_list_are_the_same_in_every_pose_at_finite_theta`),
so ISLA-DTT is pose-invariant. Rounding can break this in two places. The
frame can tie: two equal principal variances, or an axis without a third
moment, whose sign then follows whichever of the dataset's axes it overlaps
most. There a rigid motion can regroup the clusters, and the read moves
only at the size of the tree's error, which vanishes as $\theta \to 0$. So
can the octant split, at a normal component that is zero but for rounding
in that frame: its sign, and so the cell's tree, then rests on rounding.

**On the lug, rounding decides the octant of most cells and the box test of
many pairs, in float32 as in bfloat16.** The lug's faces are parallel to its
principal axes, so most of its normals have components that are exactly zero
in the forest's frame, and the stored ones are rounding residues: 86% of the
lug's cells (the median over 24 test cases, 78 to 90%) have a smallest
component below the bound on its rounding error from the cell's float32
vertices, so the sign test that picks their octant reads rounding, natively
as well as posed. Posed against native, 11% of the cells (4 to 20%) change
octant and every point's list changes; built with the native octant labels,
the posed forest gives 94% of the points their native list back. Most of the
rest are exact ties of the box test: the lug's prediction points are its
hexahedral mesh's nodes, commensurate with its boundary cells, so at
$\theta = 1$ the test is an exact equality for many pairs, and a change of
$\theta$ by a factor $1 \pm 10^{-6}$ changes 6.7% of the lists, against
0.001% on AirfRANS. ISLA-DTT's posed error on the lug, scored in float32 at
$\theta = 1$, is 1.53 and 1.98 times its native error (seeds 42 and 43),
the posed lists hold 1.29 times the pairs, and at $\theta = 0$, where no
cluster forms, posed and native agree to $10^{-4}$. The frame is not the
cause: the normalized third moments of its two nearly symmetric axes, about
$10^{-6}$, move under pose by at most $1.1 \times 10^{-7}$, so the code's
tie threshold of $10^{-9}$ decides no sign. On the AirfRANS interior task with
the airfoil alone no normal has a component below $10^{-5}$, 0 to 8 cells
change octant, and posed equals native to 0.25% at every opening angle, with
the same pair counts (results/campaigns_2026-10-23/dtt_pose/MECHANISMS.md, sections 1 and 3;
results/campaigns_2026-10-23/dtt_knobs/sens/sens_table.md). With its far field
it ties as the lug does: the far field's straight edges lie along the
forest's axes, so one component of each normal is about $2 \times 10^{-6}$;
posed against native 16 to 45% of the far-field cells (median 29%) change
octant, and ISLA-DTT trained with the far field has a posed error 1.53 to
2.52 times its native error (@sec-limits-af-whole;
results/campaigns_2026-10-23/af_whole_read/RESULTS.md, sections 1 and 3).

**A forest that depends on the boundary alone is designed and measured on a
prototype.** The design, approved by the supervisor, changes five things.
The forest is built and walked outside autocast, in the inputs' precision.
Its coordinates are taken about the boundary's measure-weighted centroid in
float64, the frame kept in float64, and rounded once. Its orientation
classes are the $2d$ faces of the cube, the axis of a normal's largest
component in the frame with that component's sign, in place of the $2^d$
sign octants; a component within twice the bound on its rounding (the
cell's own bound from its vertices, plus the frame's rotation under the
rounding of its inputs) of the largest counts as tied, and the face goes
to the lowest tied axis. The box test admits a node only when it is
separated with the arithmetic's error included, so an exact tie of the
test opens the node in every pose. And each token carries its normal's
error bound into the forest. A face holds normals with $\lvert n_k \rvert
\geq 1/\sqrt d$, the bound an octant gives, so the coherence test still
admits every node at $\theta = 1$, and a normal and its negative still land
in different trees. On the prototype, an ISLA-DTT forward with random
weights on 12 lug cases changes under pose by $1.6 \times 10^{-7}$
relative (the median; float32 roundoff), against $2.1 \times 10^{-6}$ with
the octant forest; under bfloat16 autocast the forest is bitwise the
float32 one on every case probed on the lug, AirfRANS and the DrivAerML
Volume task; a DrivAerML Volume point reads 17% fewer pairs (586 against
706); and interacting ISLA, which builds no forest, is bitwise unchanged.
No rule removes a generic residual: posing in float32 moves every input by
its rounding, so a few cells per case sit within rounding of a face's edge
or a Morton grid line, which leaves 0.52% of the pairs unmatched on the
DrivAerML Volume task (results/campaigns_2026-10-23/dtt_pose/DESIGN.md, sections 2, 3 and 6).

::: {.callout-note title="In flight"}
This limit is that of the code as it is. The forest above removes it and
changes ISLA-DTT's function; ISLA-DTT retrained with it on the lug and the
AirfRANS interior task, read for native accuracy by a registered rule, is
being measured, and the ledger (@sec-ledger) tracks it.
:::

$\theta$ is a constant of the class (`TREE_READ_THETA`), not
an argument: ISLA-DTT trains and is scored at $\theta = 1$, so its kernel,
keys and values are learned as the forest groups the cells. Read at another
opening angle, a model trained at $\theta = 1$ is less accurate, not more:
on the AirfRANS interior task and the lug, both seeds of each pair score
best at $\theta = 1$ on every field, against $\theta$ = 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75,
1.25, 1.5 and 2, and the exact read at $\theta = 0$ has 1.8 to 4.7 times
the error at $\theta = 1$. At $\theta = 1$ each layer's read differs from
the exact read on the same states by 3.9% to 27% (the median over points,
by layer, AirfRANS), mostly through the clusters' mean values, and the
difference falls slowly, as $\theta^{0.33}$ to $\theta^{0.69}$ from
$\theta = 2$ to 0.5. The leaf size matters less: leaves of 2 or 8 cells
change the AirfRANS error by at most 0.1%; on the lug leaf 2 costs 2% and
33% (seeds 42 and 43) and leaf 8 at most 0.8%
(results/campaigns_2026-10-23/dtt_knobs/sens/sens_table.md;
results/campaigns_2026-10-23/dtt_knobs/order/order_table.md). Whether a
model trained at a smaller $\theta$ is more accurate is open
(@sec-oq-dtt-theta). The tree's error
is also what moves ISLA-DTT under an exact refinement of the boundary: on
the AirfRANS interior task, with the standing's pair, trained without
compilation, splitting the airfoil's panels raises its
pressure error by `{python} f"{min(DTT_REFINE) - 1:.1%}"` to
`{python} f"{max(DTT_REFINE) - 1:.1%}"` at $\theta = 1$, and on an ISLA-DTT
pair trained under the compiled-path fault, read at $\theta = 0$, the same
refinements move its error by at most `{python} f"{DTT_THETA0:.1%}"`
(@sec-remesh-measured).

```{python}

num = lambda s: float(re.search(r"[0-9.]+(?:e[0-9]+)?", s).group(0))
floor_ = pick(cost_rows, "read-only, no read"); forest_ = pick(cost_rows, "forest, theta 1")

print(f"At 200,000 boundary cells and 200,000 prediction points (width 512, 512 slices), a point at $\\theta = 1$ reads "
      f"about {per_point.group(1)} sources, {per_point.group(2)}% of them virtual cells: "
      f"${pairs / 10 ** int(np.log10(pairs)):.1f} \\times 10^{{{int(np.log10(pairs))}}}$ pairs per layer, {dense / pairs:.0f} "
```

#### How the read runs {#sec-arch-tree-exec}

**On a GPU, every piece of the read runs a kernel that computes what its
reference computes: the same forest, the same pairs in the same order, and
the same read up to the order of summation.** A *kernel* here is one
function the GPU runs over many threads (@sec-arch-cost); Warp and Triton
are two Python frameworks for writing such kernels, which the class uses
where they are installed. Five pieces make up the read:

1. **The forest build** (`tree_build.py`, Warp) computes the frame and the
   classes with the reference's own code, then builds the trees' topology,
   boxes and node sums on the GPU. Every field of the forest is bitwise the
   reference's.
2. **The walk** (`tree_walk.py`, Warp) runs every point's walk of every
   tree in parallel: a count pass sizes the lists, a fill pass writes them,
   and the lists equal the reference's entry for entry, in its order.
3. **The pair plan** (`PairPlan`) indexes the list by point and by source
   with `torch.searchsorted` over the sorted indices, on the GPU.
4. **The read** (`fused_read.py`, Triton) computes each pair's kernel term
   from the shared basis and the block's weights inside the kernel, in the
   forward pass and again in the reverse pass, as memory-efficient
   attention kernels recompute their attention weights instead of storing
   them, so nothing per pair is kept but the basis. Its
   reverse pass sums in a fixed order and is deterministic. The basis itself,
   the small network over each pair's invariants, runs fused with those
   invariants (`fused_basis.py`).
5. **The training step runs in chunks of prediction points**
   (`ISLA.query_chunks`). The boundary side, the slice layers over the
   boundary tokens and the forest, runs once per case. The prediction
   points then run in chunks, each holding only its own activations, and
   the boundary side's reverse pass runs once after the chunks'. A loss
   that is not a sum over points, such as a relative L2 over the case,
   takes two passes when there is more than one chunk: the outputs without
   a graph, the loss's gradient in them, then each chunk recomputed with
   its reverse pass. The loss
   and every gradient are those of the unchunked step up to summation
   order, because a read-only point reads exactly what it reads among all
   of them. The recipe always trains ISLA-DTT this way. A size rule
   picks the fewest chunks of one size whose predicted peak memory fits
   the GPU: a linear function of the chunk's pairs and points, fitted to
   measured peaks on GB300 with a margin. It decides after the boundary
   side and before any point's forward pass. Under data parallelism, where
   each GPU trains on its own case and the ranks combine their gradients
   (an *all-reduce*), an all-reduce takes the smallest fitting chunk size
   over the ranks: that bounds every rank's chunks and decides one pass or
   two the same way on every rank, and a rank may then add chunks for its
   own pair counts. The step logs the choice when it changes (`_chunk_spans`
   in the recipe's `src/train.py`).

```{python}
#| label: para-arch-tree-exec
#| output: asis
# DTT-FAST: the final report's piece summary, and the integration lane's equivalence of the head against the code without
# the fast pieces, each version in its own process, on five first-batch inputs at 2,000 points (one training step)
DFR = " ".join(R.load("dtt_fast_done", "FINAL_REPORT.md").split())
SYNC_B = re.search(r"Warp forest build: every field bitwise equal; [^;]+; (\d+) host syncs down to (\d+)", DFR).groups()
SYNC_W = re.search(r"Warp walk: lists equal in the reference's order; [^;]+; (\d+) syncs down to (\d+)", DFR).groups()
assert SYNC_W[1] == "1"
BWD = re.search(r"backward is deterministic and ([\d.]+)x faster\. - A fused basis MLP with its invariants; its backward is ([\d.]+)x faster", DFR).groups()
EQ = R.md_table("dtt_fast_done", "integration/RESULTS.md", "Remerge", index=2)
assert len(EQ) == 5 and all(r_["raw"] == "True" and r_["pairs"] == "identical" for r_ in EQ)
EQ64, EQ32 = max(R.num(r_["float64"]) for r_ in EQ), max(R.num(r_["float32 ratio"]) for r_ in EQ)
BF = R.md_table("dtt_fast_done", "integration/RESULTS.md", "Remerge", index=3)
bf_o = next(r_ for r_ in BF if r_["case"] == "AirfRANS" and r_["group"] == "other")
bf_ref = [R.num(bf_o["reference family min / median / max"], i) for i in range(3)]
bf_new = [R.num(bf_o["head family"], i) for i in range(3)]
bf_b = next(r_ for r_ in BF if r_["case"] == "AirfRANS" and r_["group"] == "blocks")
bf_k = next(r_ for r_ in BF if r_["case"] == "DrivAerML vehicle" and r_["group"] == "kernel_basis")
assert all(r_["tensors above in every run / below"].startswith("0 /") for r_ in BF if r_["tensors above in every run / below"])
FAM = {r_["group"]: r_ for r_ in R.md_table("dtt_fast_done", "integration/RESULTS.md", "Remerge", index=4)}
FAM_B = [R.num(FAM["blocks max"][c]) for c in ("reference family in b1", "reference family in c1")]
PART_P = re.search(r"part P, which missed certification by (\d+) of ([\d,]+) groups", DFR).groups()
FLG = re.search(r"moves step time by ([-+\d.]+)% to ([-+\d.]+)% on the (\d+) large settings", " ".join(R.load("dtt_fast_done", "flag/REPORT.md").split())).groups()
print("**The fast pieces change no number beyond rounding.** On five real cases (the DrivAerML Volume task with the vehicle "
      "and with the whole boundary, AeroZoo, the AirfRANS interior task and the GINOT bracket lug; one training step at 2,000 "
      "prediction points with the same parameters), the class under `\"auto\"` and the same class without the fast pieces, "
      "each run in its own process, give pair lists equal entry for entry on every case. In float64 their losses, outputs "
      f"and gradients differ by at most {sci(EQ64)} relative. In float32, the fast pieces' distance to float64 is at most "
      f"{EQ32:.2f} times the reference's, against a bound of 2. In bfloat16 the test is a family of seven one-ulp "
      "perturbations of the reference's inputs, the reference's own spread under rounding, measured on the DrivAerML Volume "
      "task with the vehicle and on AirfRANS. Per tensor group the fast pieces' distance to float64 lies inside that "
      f"family's range on both, except for single-run maxima (the DrivAerML vehicle's kernel basis at "
      f"{R.num(bf_k['head family'], 2):.2f} against {R.num(bf_k['reference family min / median / max'], 2):.2f}, AirfRANS's "
      f"blocks at {R.num(bf_b['head family'], 2):.2f} in one run of seven against "
      f"{R.num(bf_b['reference family min / median / max'], 2):.2f}) and one group on AirfRANS, the remaining parameter "
      f"gradients, whose family runs {bf_new[0]:.2f} to {bf_new[2]:.2f} (median {bf_new[1]:.2f}) against the reference's "
      f"{bf_ref[0]:.2f} to {bf_ref[2]:.2f}. The supervisor accepts that read: the reference's own family moves by more than "
      "that excess between two jobs whose code differs only in a geometry change shared by both arms (its blocks' maximum "
      f"{FAM_B[0]:.2f} in one and {FAM_B[1]:.2f} in the other), no tensor lies above the reference in every run, and float64 and float32 are "
      "equivalent. The forest build synchronizes the host with the GPU "
      f"{SYNC_B[1]} times where the reference synchronizes {SYNC_B[0]}, and the walk once where it "
      f"synchronizes {SYNC_W[0]}; the read's reverse pass runs {BWD[0]} times faster than the reference's, and the "
      f"basis's {BWD[1]} times. The version and the state dict are those of the class without them. Data: "
      f"{R.source('dtt_fast_done', 'integration/RESULTS.md')} (Remerge); {R.source('dtt_fast_done', 'FINAL_REPORT.md')}.")
print()
print("**One execution attribute, `tree_read_kernel`, selects the path: `\"auto\"` (the default) or `\"reference\"`.** "
      "Under `\"auto\"` each piece checks its own requirements and logs its choice once: the build runs its Warp kernels on "
      "CUDA where Warp imports, in two or three dimensions (`resolve_tree_build`); the walk runs its Warp kernels on CUDA "
      "where the forest's depth fits the walk's stack (`resolve_walk`); and the read and its node means run fused on CUDA "
      "where Triton imports, in any precision but float64 (`ISLA.resolve_tree_read_kernel`). Any other case runs the "
      "piece's reference, and `\"reference\"` runs every reference. The reference path is the code the reference tests "
      "check and the class's whole path on the CPU; in float64 on CUDA the read and its node means run their reference, "
      "and the build and the walk keep their Warp kernels. Checkpoints do not store the attribute, and a loaded model "
      "starts at `\"auto\"`.")
print()
print("Three choices of the supervisor stand beside the fast pieces. PyTorch's default reduced-precision reduction in "
      "bfloat16 matrix products (`allow_bf16_reduced_precision_reduction`) stays on: turning it off moves the median step "
      f"time by {FLG[0]}% to {FLG[1]}% on the {FLG[2]} large settings timed and removes no measured error, since a cold "
      "compile of the bfloat16 step picks some kernels by timing, which moves the one-ulp families as much as the setting "
      "does. The read's projections stay out of the compiled blocks: compiled, they missed the certification of compiled "
      f"regions on {PART_P[0]} of {PART_P[1]} tensor groups, at the bound, although every group lies inside eager's family "
      "of one-ulp draws. And the read of bfloat16 equivalence above stands for AirfRANS; "
      "the certification of the compiled path (@sec-arch-cost) checks every dataset with families of its own. "
      f"Data: {R.source('dtt_fast_done', 'flag/REPORT.md')}; "
      f"{R.source('dtt_fast_done', 'integration/RESULTS.md')} (Pass 3, part P).")
```

One pre-registered comparison, on checkpoints of the nearest-token form
(@sec-checkpoint-form), tested a further query-independent design,
*ANCHOR*: read-only prediction points with 50,000 further interior points,
placed by a law derived from the boundary alone, that write into the slices
in the prediction points' place. @tbl-arch-dtt-evidence gives it against
interacting ISLA of the same form.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-arch-dtt-evidence
#| output: asis
ANC = RES / "campaigns_2026-10-18" / "anchor" / "readout"
SC = json.load(open(ANC / "scores.json"))
COST = json.load(open(ANC / "cost_partial.json"))
ARMS = (("isla", "interacting ISLA (control)"), ("anchor", "ANCHOR"))
FLD = (("pressure_l2", "p"), ("velocity_l2", "v"), ("nut_l2", "nut"))
err = lambda a, s, prot, f: SC[f"anc_{a}_seed{s}/{prot}"][f]
sm = lambda a, prot, f: np.mean([err(a, s, prot, f) for s in (42, 43)])
step = lambda a: np.mean([COST[f"anc_{a}_seed{s}"]["epoch250_median_s"] for s in (42, 43)])
peak = lambda a: np.mean([COST[f"anc_{a}_seed{s}"]["peak_mem_gb"] for s in (42, 43)])
posed_dev = lambda a: max(abs(err(a, s, "posed", f) / err(a, s, "native", f) - 1) for s in (42, 43) for f, _ in FLD)
DA = {}
out = ("| design | p / v / nut | ÷ interacting ISLA | both seeds below one | posed ÷ native, largest change | step at mid-run ÷ ISLA | peak memory [GB] |\n"
       "|---|---|---|---|--:|--:|--:|\n")
for a, lab in ARMS:
    vals = [sm(a, "native", f) for f, _ in FLD]
    rat = [sm(a, "native", f) / sm("isla", "native", f) for f, _ in FLD]
    below = [n for f, n in FLD if all(err(a, s, "native", f) < err("isla", s, "native", f) for s in (42, 43))]
    DA[a] = dict(rat=rat, below=below, dev=posed_dev(a), step=step(a) / step("isla"), peak=peak(a))
    out += (f"| {lab} | {' / '.join(f'{x:.5f}' for x in vals)} | {'–' if a == 'isla' else ' / '.join(f'{x:.3f}' for x in rat)} | "
            f"{'–' if a == 'isla' else (', '.join(below) or 'none')} | {100 * DA[a]['dev']:.2f}% | {DA[a]['step']:.2f} | {DA[a]['peak']:.1f} |\n")
print(out)
print(": ANCHOR against interacting ISLA on the AirfRANS uniform interior task: area-weighted relative L2 of "
      "pressure / velocity / eddy viscosity (p / v / nut), seed means of two seeds (42, 43), native meshes, float32, final "
      "checkpoints, 200 test cases, 100,000 prediction points per case. Instrument: ISLA at the reference configuration "
      "with the normalized slice reads, 500 epochs, every design trained alike; checkpoints of the nearest-token form "
      "(@sec-checkpoint-form). \"Both seeds below one\" lists the fields on which each seed of the design is below the same "
      "seed of interacting ISLA; the posed column is the largest change of a seed's error under the rotated and translated "
      "scoring, over fields and seeds; step time is the median at epoch 250 on one GB300, and peak memory as the training "
      "log reports it (rank 0). Results: results/campaigns_2026-10-18/anchor/readout/scores.json and cost_partial.json; "
      "the registered rule and its outcome: results/campaigns_2026-10-18/anchor/RESULTS.md. How to read this: a ratio "
      "compares a design with interacting ISLA, below one meaning the design is more accurate; it is not a baseline "
      "comparison.")
```

```{python}
#| label: para-arch-dtt-evidence
#| output: asis
c = DA["anchor"]
print(f"ANCHOR does not replace interacting ISLA under its registered rule ({c['rat'][0]:.3f} / {c['rat'][1]:.3f} / "
      f"{c['rat'][2]:.3f} on pressure / velocity / eddy viscosity), and it is not pose-exact (a change of up to "
      f"{100 * c['dev']:.0f}% under the posed scoring, against {100 * DA['isla']['dev']:.2f}% for interacting ISLA). It was "
```
